title: The diagonal summand of derived tensor for an extension of finite fields
statement:
Let $F\hookrightarrow B$ be an extension of finite fields [def-pc-field-extension], put $R=B\otimes_F B$ (the ordinary balanced tensor algebra), and let $\mu:R\to B$ send $b\otimes c$ to $bc$. There is an element $e\in R$ such that
$$e^2=e,\qquad \mu(e)=1,\qquad (b\otimes1-1\otimes b)e=0\quad(b\in B).$$
Let $\mathcal C$ be any site small relative to the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], and write $F_{\mathcal C},B_{\mathcal C}$ for the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal C,F)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(F_{\mathcal C}))$ and $D(\mathcal C,B)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_{\mathcal C}))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived tensor computed by K-flat resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and termwise restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For all $P,Q\in D(\mathcal C,B)$ the two coefficient actions give an $R$-action on $\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_F^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}Q$. The canonical balanced tensor morphism induces a natural isomorphism
$$e(\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_F^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}(P\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}Q)$$
in $D(\mathcal C,F)$. Here $e(-)$ means the direct summand obtained by applying $e$ termwise on compatible K-flat tensor representatives. The same assertion includes the one-point site, where these categories are $D(F)$ and $D(B)$. No boundedness or finite-dimensionality of $P,Q$ is assumed.

proof.text: Finite fields are separable. Apply Algebra.FormallyUnramified.of_isSeparable and iff_exists_tensorProduct to obtain the annihilator element with multiplication one. Tensor induction gives r e = (mu(r) tensor 1)e; taking r=e proves idempotence.

Construct both tensor presentations by site_derived_tensor_descent_independentCoefficients and its comparison through the homotopy quotient. Convert site-flatness to categorical flatness by siteSheafTensorRightIso. Transport the tensor comparison explicitly along totalFunctor_eq_mathlib; the canonical model is exactly the existing totalization.
Restriction preserves representatives by the all-constant-field-complexes-flat-and-K-flat truncation argument. Exact restriction has the standard derived factorization.
Apply the separate chain-level separability retraction to the chosen element e. This gives the natural action, canonical balanced map and section with both split identities.

The representative inclusion into the homotopy representative class is full and essentially surjective. Combine this with the bijectivity clause of the site tensor-descent theorem to obtain fully faithful precomposition from pairs of chain representatives. Transport the chain action and retraction through both presentation comparisons and descend them by the generic action-descent lemma. Evaluating its normalization squares gives exactly sourceComparison and targetComparison.
